newsitem.title: USA: Goldman's Cohen sees near-term stock 'impediments'.
newsitem.headline: Goldman's Cohen sees near-term stock 'impediments'.

text.p: U.S. stocks may run into some near-term "impediments" to further sharp gains, Abby Joseph Cohen, co-chairman of Goldman Sachs's investment policy committee, said on Wednesday.
"Equity prices may encounter some time-related impediments," Cohen, a closely followed market bull, said in a report on U.S. portfolio strategy.
Cohen said "hinderances to further dramatic price increases in the short-term" include the potential interest rate increase at the May 20 meeting of the Federal Reserve's policy-making committee.

Cohen also cited the need to wait for investors to be willing to shift their focus to 1998 corporate earnings, which usually happens in the fall. She also listed the current "dearth of details" on the U.S. budget accord announced last Friday.

Cohen noted that stock prices have now totally recovered from the March-April slump, driven by evidence of sound corporate profits, a U.S. economy growing, but at a decelerating pace, and signs inflation remains under control.

"Most recently, equity investors have been encouraged by the budget accord, believing that a capital gains tax cut will occur," the report said. "We agree that it has become more likely, although the specific legislation has not yet been crafted."
She noted many critical details of the accord are still unknown, including economic assumptions, specific tax changes and spending adjustments.
After closing at a record high 7225 on Tuesday, the Dow was off 61 points at 7164 in early afternoon trading Wednesday.
